title: Rebuttal experts in patent litigation: scope, reports, and challenges
summary: Learn how to scope and review rebuttal expert reports in U.S. patent litigation, from Rule 26 timing to depositions, Rule 702, and late-opinion risks.
body_markdown:
A rebuttal report can narrow a patent case to the real technical or economic dispute. It can also create a late-disclosure fight that eclipses the merits. Patent teams therefore need to review two paths at once: the expert's response to the opening opinion and the procedural path that makes the response timely, complete, and admissible.


**Scope note:** The discussion is limited to U.S. federal patent litigation. The scheduling order, local patent rules, contentions, and controlling circuit law govern the live matter. Litigation counsel and the expert retain responsibility for the final analysis and work product.


## Key takeaways


- A rebuttal expert responds to evidence on the same subject matter. Broad labels such as infringement, invalidity, or damages do not define the permissible scope.
- The scheduling order controls. Rule 26's 30-day period applies only when no stipulation or court order supplies a different sequence.
- New data and a different method can be proper when they genuinely contradict an opening opinion. A new claim construction, prior art combination, infringement theory, or defense presents a different problem.
- Rebuttal status does not relax Federal Rule of Evidence 702. The proponent must demonstrate to the court, more likely than not, that the testimony meets the rule’s requirements, including a sufficient basis, reliable method, and reliable application.
- Depositions, Rule 702 motions, and Rule 37 remedies should be planned from the paragraph-level scope map, not treated as separate projects.


## What is a rebuttal expert?


A rebuttal expert offers specialized testimony directed at an opposing expert's disclosed evidence. In federal practice, the defining question is functional: does the proposed testimony solely contradict or rebut evidence on the same subject matter?


The witness may be the same person who served an opening report or an expert retained for the responsive assignment. The label does not decide the report's scope. The actual opening opinions, governing order, burdens of proof, and report sequence do.


A retained or specially employed rebuttal expert generally owes the full written report required by[Rule 26(a)(2)(B)](https://www.uscourts.gov/sites/default/files/document/federal-rules-of-civil-procedure.pdf#page=59) . That means a complete statement of opinions and their bases, facts or data considered, supporting exhibits, qualifications and publication history, prior testimony, and compensation. A witness covered by Rule 26(a)(2)(C) receives a different disclosure. Rebuttal timing applies to both categories, but their disclosure requirements remain distinct.


## Start with the governing sequence


[Rule 26(a)(2)(D)](https://www.uscourts.gov/sites/default/files/document/federal-rules-of-civil-procedure.pdf#page=60) makes the court-ordered sequence primary. Only absent a stipulation or court order does the default apply: evidence intended solely to contradict or rebut evidence on the same subject matter must be disclosed within 30 days after the other party's disclosure.


*Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(a)(2)(D), official U.S. Courts text.*


Before assigning or reviewing a rebuttal report, identify:


- the opening, rebuttal, reply, and expert-discovery deadlines;
- which party bears the burden on each issue;
- any limits in the scheduling order or local patent rules;
- the operative claim constructions and current contentions;
- whether further report rounds require consent or leave; and
- the deposition and Rule 702 briefing sequence.


This sequence can differ materially among patent cases. Some orders align opening reports with burdens of proof. Some authorize a reply round on defined subjects. Others allow only opening and rebuttal reports. The word “rebuttal” cannot add a report round the order did not authorize.


## “Same subject matter” requires a precise map


Courts often compare the challenged rebuttal against the opening report at the paragraph, calculation, or exhibit level. *TCL Communications Technology Holdings Ltd. v. Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson* is a useful example. The court relied heavily on a map connecting rebuttal material to opening paragraphs, pages, and exhibits. It also held that an expert may use[independent analysis or a different methodology](https://www.finnegan.com/a/web/269758/814cv00341-TCLCommunications-v-LMEricsson.pdf) to address the same problem. Portions addressing new areas or the rebutting party's own affirmative defenses were stricken.


That distinction is narrower than a shared topic. In[FTC v. Qualcomm](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCOURTS-cand-5_17-cv-00220/pdf/USCOURTS-cand-5_17-cv-00220-8.pdf) , a report about important third-party patents did not rebut an opening opinion about important Qualcomm patents. Both propositions could be true at once. “Cellular technology” was too broad an umbrella because the proposed response did not contradict the opinion actually offered.


Patent cases make this boundary especially important. In[Brandt v. Honnecke](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCOURTS-cod-1_15-cv-02785/pdf/USCOURTS-cod-1_15-cv-02785-9.pdf) , an opening infringement opinion did not open the door to rebuttal opinions on patent prosecution, invalidity, unenforceability, or inequitable conduct. Those were different subjects despite their connection to the same patent dispute.


The practical review unit is therefore the disclosed opinion, not the case category. Create a scope map with one row for each rebuttal opinion:


Rebuttal item Opening target Proposed contradiction Scope and disclosure check


Paragraph, calculation, test, or exhibit Exact opinion and locator Why both propositions cannot stand, or how the response tests the opening method Same subject, burden, contentions, deadline, and Rule 702 basis


If the “opening target” cell can name only a broad issue such as damages, the connection is probably underdeveloped. If the proposed contradiction merely adds context that can coexist with the opening opinion, it may be an affirmative opinion in disguise.


## What proper patent rebuttal can address


Proper rebuttal can use contrary evidence, expose a missing premise, recalculate an input, test the opening method, or explain why the stated reasoning does not support the conclusion. The response must stay tied to the opinion placed in issue.


### Infringement and non-infringement


A technical rebuttal may challenge whether cited source code, testing, product documentation, or testimony establishes a claim limitation. It may apply an alternative test to the same accused operation. It should identify the relevant product version and configuration, use the operative claim construction, and explain how the evidence changes the limitation-level conclusion.


High-risk additions include a new accused feature, claim construction, doctrine-of-equivalents theory, divided-infringement defense, or product configuration absent from the disclosures that govern the case. In[Janssen Pharmaceuticals, Inc. v. Mylan Laboratories Ltd.](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/23-2042.OPINION.3-28-2025_2489646.pdf) , a divided-infringement defense first appearing in a rebuttal report was rejected as untimely where it had not been disclosed in the contentions and no amendment was sought.


### Invalidity and validity


A validity rebuttal may show that a cited reference lacks a limitation, dispute the opening expert's reason to combine references, test an asserted expectation of success, or answer a secondary-considerations opinion. It may use additional evidence to expose a flaw in the opening analysis when that evidence addresses the same question.


Watch for a new prior art combination, priority theory, person-of-ordinary-skill definition, or claim construction. Those additions can alter the invalidity case rather than answer it. A clean[claim chart](https://www.tryandai.com/product/claim-charts) can help keep the rebuttal tied to the same limitations and cited disclosures, but the expert still must explain the technical reasoning and own the opinion.


### Damages


A damages rebuttal may challenge apportionment, comparability, royalty inputs, the damages period, sales data, or the opening expert's calculations. It can use another method when the method addresses the same damages proposition.[Omega Patents, LLC v. CalAmp Corp.](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/20-1793.opinion.9-14-2021_1833974.pdf) also shows why the challenge must target the opinions at issue: the Federal Circuit held that excluding timely rebuttal critiques was improper where the Daubert motion had not challenged the expert's qualifications or comparable-license critique.


## Review the rebuttal report in eight passes


### 1. Fix the operative record


Collect the opening report, appendices, exhibits, relied-on data, claim constructions, contentions, discovery responses, and governing orders. Use stable versions and locators. Scope review fails when teams compare drafts from different record dates.


### 2. Map every responsive opinion


Connect each rebuttal conclusion to the exact opening proposition it contradicts. Record the opening paragraph, calculation, chart row, or exhibit. Then state the contradiction in one sentence. This step exposes material that shares a topic without answering an opinion.


### 3. Compare burdens and affirmative theories


Ask whether the rebutting party bears the burden on the proposed point. *TCL* allowed a party without the burden to wait for rebuttal even when it anticipated the subject, but it required affirmative-defense opinions to appear in the opening round. The governing order and forum authority still control that issue.


### 4. Reconcile the party's own disclosures


Compare the rebuttal against the same expert's opening report and deposition, as well as contentions and interrogatory responses. Flag reversals, new claim meanings, new prior art combinations, new accused instrumentalities, and rationales that repair an earlier omission.


### 5. Test the basis and method


Apply[Rule 702](https://www.uscourts.gov/sites/default/files/2025-02/federal-rules-of-evidence-dec-1-2024_0.pdf#page=30) to each opinion: helpful specialized knowledge, sufficient facts or data, reliable principles and methods, and reliable application. The proponent must demonstrate each requirement to the court under the rule’s more-likely-than-not standard. In the en banc[EcoFactor, Inc. v. Google LLC decision](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/23-1101.OPINION.5-21-2025_2518737.pdf) , the Federal Circuit treated the sufficiency of an expert's basis and reliable application as admissibility questions, separate from credibility and weight.


### 6. Check completeness and source fidelity


Verify calculations from the disclosed data. Read quotations in context. Confirm patent numbers, claim identifiers, product versions, dates, and exhibit references. Make sure the reasoning appears in the report rather than only in an attorney comment, spreadsheet, or anticipated deposition answer.


### 7. Plan the deposition from the map


[Rule 26(b)(4)(A)](https://www.uscourts.gov/sites/default/files/document/federal-rules-of-civil-procedure.pdf#page=62) permits deposition of a disclosed testifying expert after a required report is provided. Use the scope map to test what the expert understood, considered, did, and changed. Preserve the distinction between a disagreement with the conclusion and a missing or unreliable analytical step.


### 8. Assess remedy and prejudice


[Rule 37(c)(1)](https://www.uscourts.gov/sites/default/files/document/federal-rules-of-civil-procedure.pdf#page=82) bars use of undisclosed information or a witness unless the failure was substantially justified or harmless, and it permits other sanctions. The relevant factors and their application vary by circuit. Analyze surprise, the lost opportunity for expert discovery, available cure, schedule disruption, importance, and the explanation for delay under the controlling law.


## Rebuttal status does not answer admissibility


A report can fit Rule 26(a)(2)(D)(ii) and still fail Rule 702. Scope and reliability are separate gates. The report should identify the facts or data used, explain the method, and show how the expert applied that method to the actual patent record.


This matters when the dispute turns on claim construction. In[Trudell Medical International Inc. v. D R Burton Healthcare, LLC](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/23-1777.OPINION.2-7-2025_2465245.pdf) , the Federal Circuit found both disclosure and reliability problems with non-infringement testimony. The expert's analysis was untethered from the district court's claim constructions, providing an independent Rule 702 basis for exclusion.


A motion should identify the challenged opinion and ground with similar precision. A blanket attack can miss admissible critiques that were properly disclosed. The paragraph-level report map can become the working index for deposition outlines, motions to strike, Rule 702 briefing, and responses.


## Do not use supplementation as an extra report round


[Rule 26(e)](https://www.uscourts.gov/sites/default/files/document/federal-rules-of-civil-procedure.pdf#page=64) requires timely correction when a disclosure becomes materially incomplete or incorrect, and the duty extends to report and deposition information. It does not create a rolling right to improve an opinion after seeing the other side's response.


In[Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corp. v. Actavis, Inc.](https://www.ded.uscourts.gov/sites/ded/files/opinions/12-366_0.pdf) , the court explained that a report answering an opposing expert was rebuttal or reply material, rather than Rule 26(e) supplementation. In[Wavetronix LLC v. Iteris, Inc.](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCOURTS-txwd-6_21-cv-00899/pdf/USCOURTS-txwd-6_21-cv-00899-1.pdf) , unauthorized post-deposition surrebuttal reports were stricken because Rule 26 does not create a never-ending sequence of responses.


If genuinely new information makes a report materially incomplete or incorrect, disclose the correction promptly and follow the order. If the proposed change adds a method, theory, or response, analyze whether leave is required.[BearBox LLC v. Lancium LLC](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/23-1922.OPINION.1-13-2025_2449602.pdf) affirmed exclusion where a late supplemental report went beyond elaboration or clarification.


## Make the rebuttal record reviewable before service


A defensible rebuttal starts with a precise opening target. From there, the expert needs a traceable record, a stated method, and reasoning that explains the contradiction. Counsel needs the parallel record of scope, timing, contentions, deposition opportunity, and potential prejudice. Keeping both paths visible makes later challenges easier to evaluate on their actual merits.
